bib.title: GRIT: Teaching MLLMs to Think with Images
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2025 (39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: Can an MLLM be taught by reinforcement learning to interleave natural-language reasoning with explicit bounding boxes (thinking with images) without reasoning-chain or box annotations?
hypothesis: Rewarding answer accuracy and output format alone (no box or chain labels) is enough for an MLLM to unify its separate grounding and reasoning abilities in one generated trace.
contributions: GRIT, a grounded reasoning paradigm where chains interleave natural language with bounding box coordinates
GRPO-GR, an RL algorithm with format, counting and GPT-aided answer rewards needing only image-question-answer triplets
Evaluations showing Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3 unify grounding and reasoning

method.summary: GRPO-GR fine-tunes Qwen2.5-VL-3B and InternVL3-2B on 20 image-question-answer triplets, with rewards for think/rethink token format, presence of at least one regex-valid box, optional box-count match, and GPT-4o-judged answer correctness. No pixels of the cropped boxes are re-fed; the model reuses its own understanding of coordinates.
method.task: visual question answering with grounded chain-of-thought via RL (GRPO)

datasets.name: Training set (VSR + TallyQA)
datasets.size: 20 image-query-answer triplets (also 500 and 7,000 variants for the scaling study)
datasets.split: 10 VSR + 10 TallyQA; TallyQA counts uniformly 0 to 4
datasets.source: VSR (Liu et al. 2023), TallyQA (Acharya et al. 2019)
datasets.preprocessing: Ablation uses 20 VSR and no counting reward

datasets.name: VSR eval
datasets.split: from the VSR subset of Visual CoT benchmark, ambiguous answers filtered manually

datasets.name: GQA eval
datasets.split: Visual CoT GQA subset, manually filtered

other.use: answer reward, eval judge, cross-modal correlation judge

training.objective: GRPO-GR: group-normalised advantage A_i=(r_i-mean)/(std+delta), delta=1e-8; clipped GRPO objective with KL penalty to reference policy; reward r = r_format + optional r_count + r_ans
training.regularisation: KL penalty beta (value not stated); clip epsilon (value not stated)
training.compute: inferred: about 96 A100-hours per model, from 8 GPUs x 12 hours

other.r_format: s_st (0.5 for think pair + 0.5 for rethink pair) + s_bf (0.5 if at least one regex-matched integer quadruplet)
other.r_count: 0.5 if number of boxes equals ground-truth count (TallyQA samples only)

inference.prompting: fixed prompt suffix appended in training and inference (also used for the CoT baseline); see prompts

other.attention_study: 100 random GQA samples, first 50 generated tokens

metrics.name: GPT-as-judge answer accuracy (ACC)
metrics.definition: score from 0 to 1 given by GPT-4o comparing predicted and ground-truth answer

metrics.name: Grounding IoU (GIoU)
metrics.definition: IoU between union of all generated boxes and union of ground-truth boxes

metrics.name: Vision-Language Reasoning Cross-Modal Correlation
metrics.definition: GPT-4o picks which of two images (generated boxes vs equal number of random boxes) matches the masked reasoning text; mean and std over 3 repeats

baselines: One-shot ICL with a fixed exemplar trace
eval.protocol: Single training run per configuration; no seeds or significance tests reported; GPT-4o judge for accuracy; human baseline of 20 hand-written grounded chains for correlation metric.

availability.code: stated 'All code, data, and checkpoints will be released'; project page https://grounded-reasoning.github.io

prompts.purpose: Grounded reasoning suffix for training and inference
prompts.text: First, think between <think> and </think> while output necessary coordinates needed to answer the question in JSON with key ’bbox_2d’. Then, based on the thinking contents and coordinates, rethink between <rethink> </rethink> and then answer the question after <answer>.

prompts.purpose: GPT-4o answer judge and answer reward

prompts.text:
Please decide which image has the bounding boxes that match the following description: {$grounded_reasoning_masked}
Reply with exactly "Image 0" or "Image 1".

limits: Only small models (3B, 2B) tested because of limited resources; no full-scale scaling.
Out-of-domain gains grow slowly with more data; authors say data diversity matters more than volume.
Gap remains to human-written grounded chains on the cross-modal correlation metric.
Few-shot SFT beats GRIT on Qwen GQA accuracy (64.6 vs 62.8).
No seeds, variance or significance tests; KL beta, clip epsilon, decoding settings, max length not stated.
Accuracy and the correlation metric rely on GPT-4o as judge; test sets are small curated samples with manual box refinement.
Models do not always follow the JSON box format; rewards use regex only and do not check box correctness, so boxes may be off (App E example).
Counting data and reward matter: ablation lowers out-of-domain results.
